Term Loan Election (s.2.07): at least 15 days' notice to the Administrative Agent; converts ALL Advances outstanding on the Termination Date; fee 0.75%. The s.3.03 conditions must be met: all s.4.01 reps correct in all material respects, including the no-MAC-since-Dec 31, 2024 rep (last sentence of 4.01(e)), the litigation rep (4.01(f)), the ERISA reps (4.01(h)-(l)) and the environmental rep (4.01(n)), because the carve-out for those reps applies only to a Borrowing; no Default on the notice date or the conversion date; and any other approvals, opinions or documents a Lender reasonably requests. No reborrowing once term loans are prepaid.
rows.ca_quote: The Company may, upon not less than 15 days' notice to the Administrative Agent, elect (the "Term Loan Election") to convert all of the Advances outstanding on the Termination Date in effect at such time into a term loan
rows.explanation: The TS sets only a no-default condition and an unspecified notice, and its CPs to all Advances say the MAC, litigation, ERISA and environmental reps are made only on the Closing Date. The CA adds a 15-day notice period, an all-Advances conversion (the TS fee wording 'any Advances so converted' implies partial conversion was possible), and a bring-down at term-out of every rep, including MAC since Dec 31, 2024, litigation, ERISA and environmental, which are excluded for ordinary Borrowings. This could block the term-out in the stress scenario it is meant for. The TS's 'substantially similar to the Existing 364-Day Agreement' wording may explain it, but the term-out language itself sets no such condition.

rows.ts_value: Base Rate = highest of (i) Bank of America prime, (ii) Fed funds + 1/2 of 1%, and (iii) one-month Term SOFR or successor rate (floored at zero) + 1.00%; USD only. Term SOFR = forward-looking term rate for the interest period based on SOFR administered by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (no term-rate administrator such as CME is named), floor zero; USD only. EURIBOR from the applicable Bloomberg screen two business days before the period, floor zero; EUR only. No credit spread adjustment.

rows.ca_value: Base Rate = highest of (a) Federal Funds Rate + 1/2 of 1%, (b) Bank of America prime rate and (c) Term SOFR + 1.00%, using one-month Term SOFR for Base Rate purposes. Term SOFR (CME-administered Term SOFR Screen Rate) is set two U.S. Government Securities Business Days before the period, floor zero. EURIBOR (Alternative Currency Term Rate) is from the Bloomberg screen two TARGET Days before the period, floor zero. The CA adds a zero floor on the Federal Funds Rate, and removes the Term SOFR leg from the Base Rate when it is used as the fallback under s.2.19. No credit spread adjustment.
rows.ca_quote: equal to the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 1/2 of 1%, (b) the rate of interest in effect for such day as publicly announced from time to time by Bank of America as its "prime rate" and (c) Term SOFR plus 1.00%.

TS: "Honeywell International Inc. Summary of Terms and Conditions - $3,000,000,000 364-Day Multi-Currency Revolving Credit Facility". It is an indicative, undated 10-page term sheet (footer "2026 Honeywell Term Sheet"), and page 10 is the 364-Day Pricing Grid. The TS says documentation will be "substantially similar" to the Existing 364-Day Credit Agreement dated March 17, 2025. In the layout extraction of TS pages 2-9 the left-column headings are out of line with the body text (for example "Commitment Fee:" and "Interest Rates and" sit inside the Commitment Reduction paragraph). Each paragraph was mapped to its heading by order, and quotes were taken only from clean text runs. CA: a new, stand-alone agreement, not an amendment. It is the 364-DAY CREDIT AGREEMENT dated as of March 6, 2026 (Exhibit 10.1, Execution Version) among Honeywell International Inc. as Company, the Initial Lenders, and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent, with Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding and MUFG as Syndication Agents (the TS names only GS and MS; a party point for another group). The file has 113 PDF pages, ending with the signature pages (PDF p.81-113). The table of contents section numbering in the text extraction is misaligned (for example it shows s.2.13 as [Reserved]); section references here follow the body text. Limitations: (1) Schedule I (Commitments), Schedule 9.02 and Exhibits A-D appear in the table of contents but are NOT in the CA file. Per-lender and total commitments could therefore not be tied to Schedule I; the $3,000,000,000 total is taken from the cover page. (2) The CA Applicable Margin grid (PDF page 9) is garbled in the layout text, but level-by-level values were re-confirmed in review against the layout fragments and the TS grid: margins 0.50/0.625/0.75/0.875/1.00/1.125% and commitment fees 0.020/0.030/0.040/0.050/0.075/0.090%, with identical rating thresholds (AA-/Aa3, A+/A1, A/A2, A-/A3, BBB+/Baa1, below). Main findings: the economics (amount, currencies, margin and fee grids, term-out fee, day counts, minimum amounts, 103% currency test, Spin-Off step-down to $2bn) reconcile. The differences: the CA term-out requires a full rep bring-down, including MAC, litigation, ERISA and environmental reps that the TS limits to the Closing Date, plus 15 days' notice and conversion of all Advances (material, lender-favourable); a split-rating rule and no-rating default to Level 6; default interest extended to overdue interest and fees; a shorter Term SOFR borrowing notice (2 Business Days against 3 in the TS); an added non-ratable commitment reduction right (s.2.06(c)), with the Rating Condition attached to it rather than to lender replacement as in the TS; small borrower-favourable mechanics on the $3,500 replacement/assignment fee (assignee may pay; Agent may waive); and a 60-day borrowing suspension after a Change of Control.
